notes.title: Patch 1.01
notes.notes: [p]Fixed a few minor issues:[/p][list][*][p]Added a fade transition from the “About Developer” menu to the main menu[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a display bug in the “About Developer” screen on 16:10 aspect ratio[/p][/*][*][p]The “Continue” button is now only available after reaching level 2 — this way, the first story beat isn’t skipped and it feels more natural[/p][/*][/list][p]Thanks a lot to everyone who’s playing! notes.title: The full version is out!
notes.notes:
[p]The full version is out!

I still can’t quite believe I’m writing this — this is my first game, and I made it entirely solo. The last few days were especially intense: final translations, builds, bug fixes…[/p][p]Thank you so much to everyone who wishlisted the game and followed the journey — your support truly kept me going. If you get a chance to play, I’d be incredibly grateful for a review or even just a quick message.[/p][p]The game is 10% off during launch week. Hope you like it![/p][p][/p][p]Tim[/p]

notes.title: Leo: The Square launches on Steam on June 17!
notes.notes: [p]Hi everyone![/p][p][/p][p]The past few months have been quite difficult — life kept getting in the way, and there wasn’t much time for development. Still, I decided not to postpone the release and am officially announcing the release date of [b]Leo: The Square[/b] — [b]June 17![/b][/p][p]This project started over a year ago as something small. Then came long breaks, and it stretched out much more than I expected. Steam Next Fest helped me get back into development, release the demo, and gave me the confidence to see it through. I also set a release date for myself so I wouldn’t keep pushing it back in my mind. Now I’m working hard to make sure the final result is worth it![/p][p]After release, I plan to continue supporting the game — adding updates, new localizations, and levels. I already have lots of ideas I haven’t had time to implement yet. That said, [i]Leo: The Square[/i] will be a complete project at launch.[/p][p]I’m really happy with how the latest levels turned out — they feel different in style, don’t repeat themselves, and stay fresh. I hope you’ll feel the same when you play.[/p][p][/p][p]Tim[/p]

notes.title: Getting Closer to Release!
notes.notes:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

[b]I wanted to share a quick update[/b] - I’ve been actively working on the game, and as of now, about two-thirds of the levels are complete. The release is getting closer. Just recently, I finished working on a unique level that stands out from the rest of the game.

To be honest, the closer I get to the finish line, the harder it is to believe I’ll actually complete it. That’s why I’ve now set an internal release date for myself. I’m not sharing it publicly just yet — anything can happen - but I’m doing my best to meet it.

[b]I started this project a long time ago[/b], but life kept getting in the way, and it took me a while to really focus. Now I finally feel like I’m on the final stretch, which is also the hardest part. Even though the game is small, it means a lot to me - it’s my first game. Some of you may have already played the demo, and it’s still available!

[b]Sometimes it’s hard to believe that someone else will actually play this game[/b], or that it will really be sold on Steam… but I’m doing everything I can to make that happen. I’m both excited and nervous about that moment. But I’m sure it’s going to be fun.

[b]Thank you so much for following the project![/b]

notes.title: Demo Update: Save System, Level Select & Fixes
notes.notes:
[b]Demo Version Updated![/b]

This update brings a set of improvements to make the experience smoother and more complete:

[list]
[*] Added a save system
[*] You can now start a new game or continue from where you left off
[*] Level selection is now available from the main menu
[*] Checkpoints have been added to tougher sections
[*] Screen fade-in/out effect added when starting the game
[*] Several minor bugs fixed
[/list]

[b]Thanks to everyone who played and shared feedback![/b]
This update makes the demo feel much closer to the final version. Try it out and let me know what you think!

Play demo: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3542470/Leo_The_Square_Demo/

notes.title: Demo Version is Out!
notes.notes:
The demo version of Leo: The Square is now live and open to everyone! 

This demo includes 9 handcrafted levels with a meditative gameplay experience, focusing on platforming mechanics and obstacle-solving. While it doesn’t include story elements yet, it fully represents the core feel of the game. The demo also features atmospheric music and sound design, carefully crafted to match the minimalist aesthetic.

I’d love to hear your thoughts! Your feedback will help improve the final version, so feel free to leave a review or comment on the Steam page. And of course, don’t forget to add the game to your wishlist if you like it!

Try the demo now: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3542470/Leo_The_Square_Demo/

Hope you enjoy it!

notes.title: Demo Coming Soon to Steam Next Fest!
notes.notes:
Hello!

I'm back to developing [b]Leo: The Square[/b] after a break. The game will participate in the upcoming [b]Steam Next Fest.[/b] I'm currently working on a demo, which will be available very soon.

I'll share more details about the demo's content later. For now, I just wanted to let you know that development is ongoing, and this project is moving forward. I believe the demo will give you a better understanding of what this game is all about.

This will be my first experience releasing something on Steam, and I hope everything goes well. It's like a small rehearsal before the full release. Plus, it will help the game reach a wider audience. I'm also starting work on the trailer and other materials. There’s a lot of news ahead!

Thank you for your interest in the project!

[b]Antantic[/b]

notes.title: THE FIRST TEN LEVELS ARE READY!
notes.notes:
Hello,

I'm pleased to announce a significant milestone in the game development process. I've completed the creation of the first ten levels! It's been a long and intensive process, full of trials and creative solutions.

My friends have started testing the levels, and I'm happy to report they are satisfied with what they see. Their feedback helps to improve the gaming experience and make each level even more engaging. This is important because I aim to create a game that brings enjoyment and challenge to players.

The experience gained from working on these levels will be valuable for future development. The process typically involved starting each level with sketches on paper, translating ideas into the game engine editor. This process allows me to experiment with various arrangements of blocks, lighting, particle effects, and mechanics to achieve the desired gaming atmosphere.

My main task now is to refine the levels based on feedback and prepare them for the next stage of development. And of course, to continue creating new levels. I anticipate having around 30 or 40 levels in total by the end. I am particularly motivated to continue development, especially now that I can see the levels taking shape.

Stay tuned for updates to learn more about the development and future versions of the game!

Best regards,
Antantic

notes.title: Updates: Level Design Challenges!
notes.notes:
[b]I've got some exciting updates to share with you all.[/b] Recently, I've started putting my knowledge of level design into action, and let me tell you, it's been quite the journey! Building levels is both challenging and fascinating, but I'm loving every minute of it.

[b]It all starts with a simple pencil and paper.[/b] Yep, you heard it right! I sketch out my level ideas on paper first, just to get a sense of how everything will look and play out. Then, it's time to bring those sketches into Unity, the game engine I use. Seeing the levels come to life on the screen is always a blast!

[b]But the work doesn't end there.[/b] Once I've got the basics down, it's all about testing and fine-tuning. I jump into the game myself, playing through the levels, tweaking things here and there to make sure everything feels just right for you, the players. And you know who else helps out? My girlfriend! She's always up for giving the levels a whirl and giving me some honest feedback.

[b]When it comes to level design, clarity is key.[/b] I always keep that in mind. It's important to guide players without overwhelming them. I do this by carefully arranging things and playing with light and shadow. By doing that, I can gently steer players in the right direction and make sure the gameplay flows smoothly.

[b]I'm really hoping that the levels I'm creating will be enjoyable for both newcomers to platforming games and seasoned players alike.[/b] There's a little something for everyone, from tricky puzzles to hidden secrets waiting to be discovered.

But wait, there's more! I'm also working hard on some really cool YouTube videos where I'll be giving you a behind-the-scenes look at how Leo: The Square is coming to life. You'll get to see all the nitty-gritty details of the development process and maybe even sneak a peek at some exclusive content.

Keep an eye out for more updates, and don't forget to [b]subscribe to my YouTube channel[/b] so you don't miss out on any of the fun!

Channel link: https://youtube.com/@antantic_?si=7WjLyCQ8Tqk9AN1G

Catch you later, and happy gaming!

Warm regards,
[b]Antantic[/b]
